messages:
PagerBot: PAGER: high queue growth detected for gpu-serving-prod (gpuprod-main). queue_depth ↑, throttles observed, autoscaler alerts. runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/gpu-capacity.md :rotating_light:
Jordan (oncall): taking pager, jumping in. assigning @Maya for metrics, @Ronan for autoscale logs.
Maya (sre): seeing sustained enqueue spikes — queue depth ~ 18k -> 42k over 12m. GPU utilization 95-99% on gpuprod-main. autoscaler decisions show 'no-op' due to scale_limit and recent failure backoff. metric links: https://metrics/gpuprod-main/queue_depth, https://metrics/gpuprod-main/gpu_util
Ronan (infra): checking autoscaler controller logs, found repeated "scale_decision_suppressed: recent_provision_failures" entries. snippet:
```
2026-03-15T02:00:12Z controller INFO scale_decision_suppressed reason=provision_error count=3 last_error="insufficient_quota"
2026-03-15T02:02:05Z controller WARN backoff active until 2026-03-15T02:10:00Z
```
Quota failures look like cloud API returning 429/limit. Also see a bunch of batchconfig rollouts 02:00-02:05 altering continuous batching params and prefix cache TTL. rolling config id: cfg-a9f3b2 -> applied 02:01.
Jordan (oncall): attempted manual scale: `redwoodctl scale gpuprod-main --replicas 12` -> cloud API rejected: "quota_exceeded". So autoscaler can't add nodes and manual scale blocked.
Maya (sre): correlating timeline: at 02:01 we deployed new batching profile that tightened continuous_batch_window from 250ms -> 25ms and reduced prefix_cache_ttl from 60s -> 2s. That increased KV cache churn and reduced effective batching aggregation. Result: more small requests, less batching, more GPU load per token. Candidate rollback: revert to cfg-7d2c1e (previous continuous_batch_window=250ms, prefix_cache_ttl=60s).
Ronan (infra): I can revert config on serving pool quickly. executing rollback now. cmds:
```
redwoodctl config rollback gpuprod-main --from cfg-7d2c1e
redwoodctl config apply gpuprod-main --prefix-cache enabled --prefix-cache-ttl 60s --continuous-batch-window 250ms
```
Applying...
Ronan (infra): applied rollback and re-enabled prefix cache. triggered prefix cache warmup and explicit flush to clear stale partial keys: `redwoodctl cache flush gpuprod-main --prefix`
PagerBot: automated note: cache warmup triggered, expected warmup window ~ 90s.
Maya (sre): monitoring — queue depth peaked at 42k, after rollback queue depth 5m -> 18k, after prefix cache warmup 10m -> 6.2k. GPU util dropping from 98% -> 72% within 7 minutes. Throttles (5xx token throttles) trending down.
Jordan (oncall): manual mitigation summary: rollback batching config + re-enable prefix cache + flush. could not scale due to cloud quota. autoscaler backoff remains but with lower load will recover; will monitor for any further provision_attempt errors.
Eli (product-ops): drafting customer impact note for status page. suggested blurb:
"We observed degraded inference throughput and elevated latencies for some workloads on gpu-serving-prod between 02:00–02:12 UTC due to a configuration change to batching and prefix cache parameters. We reverted the change; services are recovering. Some customers may have seen increased latency or throttling during the window. Root cause investigation in progress."
Nina (cust-success): which customers saw the hit? need list to proactively reach out.
Maya (sre): preliminary impact: 5 enterprise tenants had requests queued > 30s and experienced error spikes: tenant IDs -> [acme-inc, bluewave, solara-ml, venturelabs, clouddesk]. exact RPC failures are being compiled. SLOs: p95 latency for generation increased from 320ms -> 1.6s for affected models during window.
Jordan (oncall): notifying SRE lead and scheduling postmortem. severity: Sev2 (partial production impact, multiple customers affected). owners: Maya (SRE) lead for RCA, Ronan (Infra) lead for autoscaler/cloud quota path, Eli for external comms, Nina for customer outreach.
Ronan (infra): follow-up: opened cloud ticket for quota exhaustion (TKT-8842) requesting temporary quota bump while we validate autoscaler behavior. Also found autoscaler backoff logic considered the failed provisioning attempts and suppressed scaling for 10m — we should tune that window and add a self-heal path when queue >> threshold.
Maya (sre): next steps in incident doc: 1) RCA + timeline 2) Postmortem with config diff and mitigation 3) small infra change: reduce autoscaler backoff when queue_depth > 25k 4) add alert to warn when batchprofile rollout changes continuous_batch_window or prefix_cache_ttl 5) add e2e test for continuous batching regression.
Jordan (oncall): marking mitigation as successful for now. will keep thread open for monitoring for another 30m. thanks all for fast response. :thumbsup:
PagerBot: PAGER RESOLVED (ack by Jordan).
